newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks jump sharply to record high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks jump sharply to record high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped to a record high of 15,370 points in early Monday morning trade in a broad-based rally that lifted blue and red chips to new highs.
The index then climbed to 15,426 for a total gain of 200 points or 1.32 percent.
"We are moving ahead now after the post-handover slump and uncertainty," said Priscilla Cheung, dealing director at Dao Hang Securities.
The Hang Seng Index saw an increase in volatility in the days straddling Hong Kong's handover to China on July 1, brokers said.
"We are also seeing a short squeeze in the futures market," said Cheung.
The July Hang Seng Index futures contract rose to a high of 15,530 in early trade then eased to trade 115 points up at 15,450.

The market was also lifted by positive sentiment generated by Wall Street's gains on Friday and the decline in June U.S. wholesale prices, pointing to a steady low inflation, low interest rate environment, brokers said.
The market shrugged off instability in regional currencies and may in fact be benefitting from the volatility, they said.
"There is some degree of safe-haven status in Hong Kong," said David Hill, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
Interest rate sensitive utilities led the market's early advance, followed by the commercial and industrial sector.
Red chips were also higher in active trade.
Hongkong Telecom leaped to an early high of HK$18.70 then eased to trade HK$0.35 higher at HK$18.50 on moderate turnover of HK$219 million.
China Light added HK$0.40 to HK$43.20. Laggard Wharf Holdings soared to HK$33.50 then fell back to trade HK$0.80 higher at HK$33.20.

Red chip China Everbright International, the most active in early trade, advanced HK$0.55 to HK$5.45 on very heavy trade of HK$468 million. The company said on Friday it was in talks to acquire a stake in a Shanghai property development.
